pages.name: Still there?
pages.task: -G1 feeds section A and -G2 feeds section B. Can you close bus-tie -Q4 now?
pages.why: Closing -Q4 would join two running sets. Unless their voltage, frequency and phase match, a large current flows the moment it closes. So they are synchronised first.

pages.name: The power map
pages.text: A [[single-line diagram]] maps a board's power, from each source through the busbars to each load. Read it in that order, sources first. The thick lines are the busbars. On the AC side, each line stands for all three phases of its cable. On the DC side, it stands for a pair of wires. An amber glow traces each line in that order, sources first.

pages.name: Live and dead
pages.text: Live lines are bold and dead lines pale. A breaker feeds everything below it, through every transformer and charger on the way. With -Q1 open, section A and everything below it are pale. Section B stays bold from -G2.

pages.alt: A single-line diagram. -G1, -G2 and the shore supply sit at the top, over the 440 V board in sections A and B. Below are the 115 V board and the 24 V DC board with battery -G3. Open: -Q1, -Q3, -Q4 and -Q23. No supply: -M1, -E1, -M4 and -M3.

pages.name: One breaker opens
pages.task: Breaker -Q12 opens. How many loads lose supply?
pages.why: -Q12 feeds transformer -T1. -T1 feeds the 115 V board. That board feeds lighting -E1 and fan -M4. So 2 loads lose supply, and the rest of section A stays live.

pages.name: Where the voltage changes
pages.text: A transformer marks where the voltage changes. Here -T1 steps 440 V down to 115 V. Charger -U1 turns 440 V AC into 24 V DC. Battery -G3 sits on the same DC board. On this sheet, a cross marks a breaker and a bar an isolator. Two circles are a transformer, and a box with ~ and = is a charger. The battery is drawn as long and short plates.

pages.task: Breaker -Q22 opens. Is the 24 V DC board still live?
pages.why: Opening -Q22 takes the charger off, so the main board no longer feeds the DC board. Battery -G3 is a source in its own right, joined through -Q5. So -E3 and -A3 stay lit, running on the battery.

pages.name: The bus-tie
pages.text: [[Bus-tie]] -Q4 joins the two sections. It is marked N.O., for normally open. So each section runs on its own set. Close it and one set can feed both. -Q2 is open and -Q4 is closed. -Q2 opened first. That left section B dead, so -Q4 could close without synchronising. Section B is bold again, fed from -G1 through the tie.

pages.name: Through the tie
pages.task: Both sets have stopped, and -Q1 and -Q2 are open. Shore breaker -Q3 is closed, so the shore supply feeds section B. You close bus-tie -Q4. What feeds pump -M1 now?
pages.answer: The shore supply, through the bus-tie
pages.why: -M1 hangs from section A. With -Q4 closed, section A joins section B, and the shore supply feeds both. A normally open breaker carries nothing across until it closes. Once closed, it carries power like any other.

pages.name: Two ways in
pages.text: Pump -M3 is fed two ways. -Q13 feeds it from section A. -Q23, marked N.O., feeds it from section B. An interlock lets only one of them close at a time. -Q13 is open and -Q23 is closed. -M3 is bold again, fed from section B.

pages.name: Lock it off
pages.task: You must work on pump -M3 and keep every other load running. Each device you lock off gets a padlock. What do you lock off?
pages.why: -M3 has two ways in. Opening -Q13 frees -Q23 to close, so both get a lock. Then every path from every source stops at a padlock. Nothing else loses supply. The drawing tells you what to lock off. Prove it dead at the pump before you start.

pages.task: Breaker -Q2 trips open. -Q3 and -Q4 stay open. How many loads lose supply?
pages.why: Section B goes dead, so pump -M2 stops. The charger stops too, but battery -G3 keeps -E3 and -A3 lit. -M3 runs from section A, and -Q23 is open. So 1 load loses supply.

pages.task: You must work on alarm panel -A3 and keep emergency lighting -E3 lit. What do you lock off?
pages.why: -A3 has one way in from its board, through -F4. Lock off -F4, and every path to -A3 stops there, from the charger and from the battery. -E3 stays lit.
